config.title: Multi-Tab Auth Sync

intro.title: Multi-Tab Auth Sync
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React application that keeps a user's login status synchronized across multiple browser tabs. You will learn how to use the browser's localStorage API and the window 'storage' event to detect and respond to changes made in other tabs. The core programming concept involves managing shared state across different instances of your app using event listeners and React hooks. You will implement this by creating a custom React hook that tracks authentication state and updates all open tabs when a login or logout occurs. This project will help you understand real-time state synchronization in a multi-tab environment using TypeScript for type safety.
intro.usecase: Multi-tab auth sync is essential in modern web applications where users open multiple tabs of the same site, such as banking dashboards, e-commerce platforms, or collaborative tools like Google Workspace. For example, logging out in one tab should immediately reflect across all open tabs to maintain security and a consistent user state. Developers implement this to prevent stale sessions, ensure data integrity in admin panels, and provide a seamless experience in applications like project management software where authentication state changes must propagate instantly.

objectives: Implement a custom React hook to manage authentication state across browser tabs
Configure event listeners to detect storage changes from other tabs
Initialize and update authentication state using localStorage as a synchronization mechanism
Bind authentication state changes to React component re-renders
Construct a login/logout UI that reflects synchronized state across multiple tabs
Integrate the multi-tab auth sync hook into a React application component
Manipulate browser storage events to trigger authentication state updates

steps.title: Import React, useState, useEffect, and useRef
steps.instruction: Import React, useState, useEffect, and useRef from the 'react' library.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to bring in multiple named exports from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple hooks from React
import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and the required hooks here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React hooks for managing state, side effects, and references are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: React, useState, useEffect, and useRef are all imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some of the required hooks, but not all. Make sure to import React, useState, useEffect, and useRef from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import React, useState, useEffect, and useRef from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the AuthSync component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named AuthSync that returns JSX. Use TypeScript typing for the component.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called AuthSync that returns a JSX element like a div.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';

// Create the AuthSync component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named AuthSync is defined with proper TypeScript typing and returns JSX.
successCriteria: The AuthSync component is defined as a function or arrow function, includes TypeScript typing, and returns a JSX element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it's named exactly 'AuthSync' and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a function named AuthSync that returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize authentication state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthSync component, use useState to create an isAuthenticated state variable initialized to false with boolean type annotation.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook with TypeScript to declare a boolean state variable. Example: const [isAuthenticated, setIsAuthenticated] = useState<boolean>(false);
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: creating a boolean state variable
const [isLoggedIn, setLoggedIn] = useState<boolean>(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a properly typed isAuthenticated state variable initialized to false.
successCriteria: isAuthenticated state is declared with useState, has boolean type annotation, and is initialized to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've declared isAuthenticated with useState, added the boolean type annotation, and initialized it to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state variable isn't properly set up. Check that you're using useState with boolean type and initial value false.

steps.title: Create a ref for channel name with useRef
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthSync component, create a ref using useRef to store the BroadcastChannel name. Initialize it with the string 'auth-sync-channel' and provide the proper TypeScript type annotation.
steps.hint: Use useRef with a generic type argument <string> to create a mutable reference that holds a string value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a ref for a string value
const channelNameRef = useRef<string>('my-channel');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a ref named channelRef (or similar) initialized to 'auth-sync-channel' with proper TypeScript typing.
successCriteria: A useRef is declared with string type and initialized to 'auth-sync-channel' inside the component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your useRef has the correct TypeScript type annotation (<string>) and is initialized with 'auth-sync-channel'.
steps.feedbackWrong: use useRef with a string type and initialize it with 'auth-sync-channel' inside the component body.

steps.title: Define the login handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your AuthSync component, create a function called loginHandler that sets isAuthenticated to true and updates tabCount by incrementing it by 1.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setIsAuthenticated with true and setTabCount with the current tabCount plus one.
steps.expectedOutcome: A loginHandler function is defined that updates both authentication and tab count state.
successCriteria: The loginHandler function is defined, calls setIsAuthenticated(true), and updates tabCount by incrementing it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it sets isAuthenticated to true and increments tabCount by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The login handler function is missing or doesn't properly update both state values.

steps.title: Define the logout handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your AuthSync component, define a logoutHandler function that sets isAuthenticated to false and decrements tabCount by 1.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setIsAuthenticated with false and setTabCount with tabCount - 1.
steps.expectedOutcome: A logoutHandler function is defined that updates both authentication state and tab count.
successCriteria: logoutHandler function is defined, calls setIsAuthenticated(false), and updates tabCount to decrement by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your logoutHandler updates both isAuthenticated and tabCount states.
steps.feedbackWrong: The logout handler function is missing or doesn't properly update both state values.

steps.title: Set up BroadcastChannel in useEffect
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthSync component, add a useEffect hook that creates a BroadcastChannel instance using the channel name from your ref and sets up a message event listener to sync authentication state across tabs.
steps.hint: The useEffect should run once on mount. Create the channel with new BroadcastChannel(channelNameRef.current) and add an event listener for 'message' events.
steps.expectedOutcome: A useEffect hook is added that initializes a BroadcastChannel and sets up a message event listener.
successCriteria: The useEffect hook is defined with an empty dependency array, creates a BroadcastChannel instance using channelNameRef.current, and adds an event listener for 'message' events.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your useEffect creates the channel with channelNameRef.current and adds the 'message' event listener.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useEffect hook for BroadcastChannel setup is missing or incorrect. Remember to create the channel and add the message event listener.

steps.title: Return the main container structure
steps.instruction: Inside your AuthSync component, return a div container with the className 'auth-sync-container'.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement (return null;) with a JSX div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a JSX container div with the correct className, ready to hold authentication UI elements.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a JSX div element with className 'auth-sync-container'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning a JSX div element with exactly the className 'auth-sync-container'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement should output a JSX div with className 'auth-sync-container'. Check your JSX syntax.

steps.title: Add authentication status display
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your AuthSync component, add a paragraph element that displays the current authentication status based on the isAuthenticated state. Use the format: 'Authentication status: [Authenticated/Not authenticated]'.
steps.hint: You can use a ternary operator to conditionally display 'Authenticated' when isAuthenticated is true, and 'Not authenticated' when false.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a paragraph displaying whether the user is currently authenticated or not.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added inside the container that displays 'Authentication status: Authenticated' when isAuthenticated is true, and 'Authentication status: Not authenticated' when false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but it doesn't correctly display the authentication status. Make sure to use the isAuthenticated state with a ternary operator to show 'Authenticated' or 'Not authenticated'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The authentication status display is missing or incorrect. Add a paragraph element that shows 'Authentication status: Authenticated' when isAuthenticated is true, and 'Authentication status: Not authenticated' when false.

steps.title: Add tab count display
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element inside the container that displays the current tabCount value with descriptive text.
steps.hint:
Use JSX to create a

element that shows the tabCount state value, similar to how you displayed the authentication status.

Current count: {count}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show both authentication status and the number of authenticated tabs.
successCriteria: A paragraph element displays the tabCount value with appropriate text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your paragraph includes the tabCount value and descriptive text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The tab count display wasn't added correctly. Check that you created a paragraph element showing the tabCount state value.

steps.title: Add login and logout buttons with click handlers
steps.instruction: Add two button elements inside the container - one for login and one for logout - and wire their onClick events to the respective handler functions.
steps.hint: Create <button> elements with appropriate text and onClick handlers that call the login and logout functions you defined earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two interactive buttons appear in the UI - one labeled 'Login' that triggers authentication, and one labeled 'Logout' that ends authentication.
successCriteria: The component contains two button elements with onClick handlers wired to handleLogin and handleLogout functions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but check that both login and logout buttons are present with correct onClick handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons are missing or not properly connected to the handler functions. Make sure you have two button elements with onClick handlers.
